subject: MAP replan: proposed compressed acceptance windows & contingency ladder
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@curohealth.com>
Cc: Alex Klein <alex.klein@curohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft MAP v2 + proposal to compress acceptance windows

Emily —

Following our check-in this morning, attached is the updated MAP (v2) with two proposal paths: 1) staggered acceptance (original cadence) and 2) compressed acceptance windows with an explicit contingency ladder. We think the compressed path recovers two weeks on the current close runway but increases short-term verification load on your side.

Quick summary of the change:
- Acceptance windows: compress acceptance windows from 10 business days -> 4 business days where automation coverage exists.
- Contingency ladder: pre-agreed rollback triggers, temporary feature toggles, and a one-week buffer for procurement approvals.
- Eval plan: I've added a companion eval-plan.xlsx that highlights minimal gating prompt sets and a smoke-test matrix.

Can you confirm whether procurement/legal can turn around the revised SOW and PO within 7 business days if we go compressed? If not, we'll rebaseline to the staggered path and propose a staggered + burst-run option.

Attachments: MAP_v2.pdf, eval-plan.xlsx

Thanks,
Rafael
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Emily Wong <emily.wong@curohealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Klein <alex.klein@curohealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@curohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP v2 + proposal to compress acceptance windows

Rafael —

Thanks for the doc. We reviewed with the clinical ops and procurement teams. High-level:
- Clinical ops: OK with compressed functional verification for the analytics paths but need full-weekend-free verification for the EHR connector (can’t certify on compressed windows).
- Procurement: cannot guarantee PO turnaround in 7 business days; their SLA is currently 12–15 business days without a priority routing agreement.

Given that, we are interested in the compressed approach for everything except the EHR connector. Suggestion: split acceptance into two lanes (analytics compressed / EHR staggered). Will that still buy us the two-week recovery?

Emily
Director, Clinical Programs
CuroHealth
emily.wong@curohealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP v2 + proposal to compress acceptance windows 

Looping in Ben and Neha for risk coverage. Key operational notes:
- If we split lanes (analytics compressed / EHR staggered) we need a clear fallback in the MAP: when EHR lags, analytics must be able to ship behind a feature flag with data degradation notes.
- We should add a Risk Register entry that quantifies customer SLA impact and a trigger for an exec-level bridge if EHR verification extends beyond 10 business days.

Ben — can you prepare a short risk register CSV with: risk_id, description, probability (low/med/high), impact (L/M/H), mitigation, owner, trigger_date? Put it in the thread (risk_register.csv).

Laura
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@curohealth.com>, Alex Klein <alex.klein@curohealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@curohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: MAP decision path + executive notice (if EHR lags past 2027-06-22)

Emily / Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick reviews. Given procurement's current SLA, and clinical ops constraints on EHR, proposed final approach:
1) Two-lane acceptance: analytics (compressed 4 business days), EHR connector (staggered 10 business days).
2) Contingency ladder: if EHR verification is not complete by 2027-06-22 (trigger_date), Redwood will:  a) enable analytics behind a customer-configured feature flag, b) spin up a 3-day exec bridge to resolve EHR test blockers, and c) offer a temporary credit (see MAP_v2.pdf, section 4.3) if go-live is materially delayed beyond agreed window.
3) Procurement ask: if CuroHealth can provide a priority PO routing (internal escalation) to reduce PO turn time to <=8 business days we will move certain non-EHR tasks earlier and avoid the exec bridge.

Next steps (please confirm by EOD Tuesday):
- Procurement: confirm PO SLA/priority path or provide expected PO date.
- Emily: confirm acceptance lanes and approve the MAP_v2 sign-off path for analytics-first enablement.
- Redwood: finalize risk_register.csv and create HubSpot deal update + DocuSign envelope.

Attachments included: MAP_v2.pdf, eval-plan.xlsx, risk_register.csv

If we do not get a commitment on the procurement priority path, we will formally rebaseline the close date in HubSpot on Friday and route an exec escalation note to both teams.

—Rafael
